# Temple Scroll Column 34 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 34 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**34:1** The chambers on the west side of the outer court shall be for the sons of Israel who come up to the temple to worship before Me.

**34:2** They shall bring their offerings, their sacrifices, their votive offerings, and their freewill offerings.

**34:3** They shall eat in these chambers — they, their sons and daughters, their menservants and maidservants.

**34:4** No foreigner shall eat of the holy things, for it is not permitted to him.

**34:5** The priests shall eat of the most holy things within the inner court; the holy things they shall eat in the chambers appointed to them in the outer court.

**34:6** Each man shall eat in his appointed place; they shall not mix one with another.

**34:7** The priests shall not carry any of the holy food from their chambers into the outer court.

**34:8** They shall not profane My holy food; for it is holy, and they shall treat it as holy.

**34:9** Any man of the sons of Israel who brings a sacrifice shall come to the gate nearest to him.

**34:10** The Levites shall receive it from his hand at the gate and bring it to the priests at the altar.

**34:11** Each man shall bring his offering to the gate appointed for his tribe.

**34:12** He shall not enter through the gate of another tribe, for each tribe has its own gate.

**34:13** The sons of Levi shall stand at the gates to receive the offerings from the sons of Israel.

**34:14** They shall bring them to the altar and to the chambers, each offering to its proper place.

**34:15** No man shall come into the outer court empty-handed before Me at the appointed feasts.

**34:16** Each man shall bring according to his ability — according to the blessing of the LORD his God that He has given him.

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus follows EMET for "sons of Israel" and "chambers," preferring the literal patronymic and the temple-specific architectural term. LOGOS's "votive offerings" preferred over EMET's "vows" for accuracy. Verse 16 echoes Deuteronomy 16:17.*
